### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/package.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/package.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82a3ed2e861d260fdd65517e6b17f03c42eb90c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `579bdb897a20b4dad1fce191865e535064ebfaa4` — the merge of head `785a7428c169810953a4d75e71f91e848409c6d4` into base `82a3ed2e861d260fdd65517e6b17f03c42eb90c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 579bdb897a20b4dad1fce191865e535064ebfaa4 && git checkout 579bdb897a20b4dad1fce191865e535064ebfaa4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 82a3ed2e861d260fdd65517e6b17f03c42eb90c2 785a7428c169810953a4d75e71f91e848409c6d4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 82a3ed2e861d260fdd65517e6b17f03c42eb90c2 && git merge --no-ff 785a7428c169810953a4d75e71f91e848409c6d4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82a3ed2e861d260fdd65517e6b17f03c42eb90c2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 82a3ed2e861d260fdd65517e6b17f03c42eb90c2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Epic red-line review: E5 #31677, connectors part, head 47f5d0c0 · 2026-11-09T00:18Z**

Verdict: **PASS**, with one fix to make before landing. The fix is a comment move, not a red-line issue, and needs no re-review.

| Red line | Reading |
|---|---|
| 1. Never loosen | The refusal runs before the desired set is built, and a refused name is skipped (`refusedNames.has`), so it is never materialized. On reload, a name that was materialized before is torn down. The older duplicate-name check stays behind it. Phase 1's one-holder refusal for `connector` is untouched, so no booted deployment changes its answer today. |
| 2. Ambiguity reported, never guessed | It uses the one resolver (`resolvePackageScopedName`, type `connector`, no caller package), with no second resolver and no first-registered fallback. `fail()` carries `refusal.message`, which names every candidate. The two-holder test pins both package ids in the message and zero provider calls. |
| 3. Independently releasable | (a) The boot answer is unchanged while phase 1 stands. (b) Seat 3's narrowing reading: D3 (a) 0, package-caller reads 0, outside-closure 0, sibling-in-artifact 0. (c) objectql moves from devDependencies to dependencies; objectql does not depend on service-automation, so there is no cycle. (d) The changeset is a patch with the affected parties stated. |

**Fix before landing:** the new `refusedDeclaredConnectorNames` JSDoc and method sit between the `[#28534]` JSDoc and `declaringPackageReadersOrNone`. That leaves the `[#28534]` block stacked above the new one, where it documents the wrong method. Move the new method and its JSDoc above the `[#28534]` block, or below `declaringPackageReadersOrNone`.

**The two points seat 3 raised:**
- `packageScopedRegistryOf` refuses nothing when the slice is absent, and `getService` errors are read as "no registry". Both match the existing `declaringPackageReadersOrNone` precedent, and both are inert today because phase 1 still refuses connector clashes. The test that uses a real `SchemaRegistry` with two holders also pins the slice shape: a rename of any slice method fails that test instead of silently disabling the check. **Accepted for this PR.**
- **Owed by the trailing backstop child that narrows phase 1 for `connector` (ADR-0150 D9):** once phase 1 no longer refuses, fail-open on a missing slice would loosen. That child must either make a composition that has an `objectql` service but no resolver slice fail closed, or show that every shipped composition carries the slice. This is recorded here so the backstop card picks it up.

**Still waiting on other cards:** webhooks wait for the Q1 `Ruled:` on #31677 (6728850663). Email waits for R2 #31716 (the bundle-addition holder fix).

Seat 3 accepts and lands this after the fix and green CI. It is not a governed surface.

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [42541734246](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42541734246) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Test Core (1/8)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42541734246/job/128918599891)** — 失败步骤: Run this shard's tests

  ```
  @objectstack/cli:test:  FAIL   integration  test/validate-namespace-name.test.ts > ADR-0150 child N — os validate and os build refuse what the package door refuses, in its words > premise: the package
    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/cli:test: AssertionError: expected BareNameConflictError: Bare-name conflict… { …(8) } to be undefined
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）

**跨 PR 相同签名（24h，按失败测试文件聚合）：**

- `test/validate-namespace-name.test.ts` — 24h 内已弹出 **3 个 PR**（#31661、#31718、#31725），但它们同属 **1 条投机栈** ⇒ **1 次独立命中**。汇总 issue：#31736（已刷新）
- ⚠️ 24h 评论账本**没读完**（超过 5 页仍未读到窗口尽头），所以上面的「不同 PR 数」是**下界**，不是全量。

**历史信号：**
- 本 PR 过去 24h 无队列失败记录（首次）。
- 过去 24h 队列共有 13 个失败构建（不含本次）。

**分诊清单：**
1. 失败测试在本 PR 改动的包里 → 真回归，修 PR。
2. 失败测试与本 PR 无关 → 看上面的「跨 PR 相同签名」；已有汇总 issue ⇒ flaky/环境问题实锤，去那张 issue 上谈，修好前重排只会再烧一轮全队列。
3. 两者都不是 → 可能与同组 PR 语义冲突；等前面的 PR 落地或失败出队后再重排一次即可，不要连续重排。
